Get the Mutations of Municipalities

Source: R/gemeinde-mutations.R
gemeindeMutationen.Rd

Returns the change history of the Swiss political municipalities between two dates: mergers, splits, creations, abolitions, renamings, renumberings and reassignments to another district. It is needed to bring data of different municipality stands onto a common stand, and to explain why a gem_id appears in one year and not in another.

Usage

gemeindeMutationen(
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  territoryExchange = FALSE,
  cache = TRUE,
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

from, to

start and end of the period, each a Date or a string "YYYY-MM-DD". The defaults are 1960-01-01, the start of the register, and today.

territoryExchange

logical; if TRUE, mutations that consist only of territory exchanges between municipalities are included.

cache

logical; if TRUE, results are read from and written to the local cache (see cacheList()).

refresh

logical; if TRUE, the source is queried again even if a cached copy exists.

Value

A data.frame with one row per predecessor-successor pair and the columns mutation_id, mutation_d, mutation_type_c, old_gem_id, new_gem_id, old_gem_x, new_gem_x, old_hist_id, new_hist_id, old_bezirk_x, new_bezirk_x, old_bezirk_hist_id, new_bezirk_hist_id, old_step_c and new_step_c. The last two are the source fields InitialStep and TerminalStep, passed through unchanged.

Details

The history comes from the AGVCH mutation service and is kept separate from the municipality stock returned by gemeinde(). Each row links one predecessor version (old_*) to one successor version (new_*) of a mutation; a merger of three municipalities therefore yields three rows sharing the same mutation_id. Several predecessors or successors are never collapsed into one field.

The service delivers no type code, so mutation_type_c is derived from the structure of each mutation:

"creation", "abolition"

no predecessor or no successor.

"merger"

several predecessors, one successor.

"split"

one predecessor, several successors.

"territory-exchange"

several municipalities that all persist.

"reorganisation"

any other many-to-many mutation.

"rename", "renumber", "reassign"

one-to-one change of name, BFS number or district; combinations are joined with a hyphen in this order, e.g. "rename-reassign".

"other"

one-to-one without a detectable change, e.g. a pure territory change when territoryExchange = TRUE.

"reassign" refers to the district version: a district that is itself renamed gives all its municipalities a new district version.

See also

gemeinde() for the stock at one date.

Other swiss.register: gemeinde(), kanton(), praemienregion(), raumgliederung()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
mut <- gemeindeMutationen(from = "2020-01-01", to = "2021-01-01")
subset(mut, mutation_type_c == "merger")
} # }
